items.text: Safety Note: Avoid skin contact with the solvents and dyes, especially if you have sensitive skin.

items.label: section_header
items.text: KEY POINT

items.label: text
items.text: If the dye does not move from the pencil line during an experiment, then the dye is not at all soluble in the solvent you are using. In this case, you need to find a different solvent. If the dye moves up the paper with the solvent front, the dye is too soluble in that solvent and, again, you have to try a different solvent.

items.text: Both liquids boil, but by careful heating you can control the temperature of the column so that all the water condenses in the column and trickles back into the flask. Only the ethanol remains as a vapour all the way to the top of the fractionating column andout into the condenser.

items.label: text
items.text: Paper chromatography can be used to separate a variety of mixtures. However, at International GCSE level we will usually use it to separate mixtures of coloured inks or food colourings. Most inks and food colourings are not just made up of one colour but contain a mixture of dyes.

items.label: text
items.text: Paper chromatography can also be used to separate a mixture of colourless substances such as sugars, but then some method must be used to make the spots visible on the paper.

items.label: section_header
items.text: ACTIVITY 2

items.label: section_header
items.text: PRACTICAL: INVESTIGATING THE COMPOSITION OF DYE WITH PAPER CHROMATOGRAPHY

items.label: text
items.text: We can investigate the composition of a mixture of coloured dyes using paper chromatography. To do this we carry out the following steps.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Draw a line with a pencil across a piece of chromatography paper; this line should be about 1 cm from the bottom of the paper. Do not use a pen as the colours in the ink may move up the chromatography paper with the solvent.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Put a spot (use a teat pipette or a capillary tube) of the mixture of dyes on the pencil line and allow it to dry.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Suspend the chromatography paper in a beaker that contains a small amount of solvent so that the bottom of the paper goes into the solvent. It is important that the solvent is below the pencil line so that the inks/colourings don't just dissolve in the solvent.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Put a lid (such as a watch glass) on the beaker so that the atmosphere becomes saturated with the solvent. This is to stop evaporation of the solvent from the surface of the paper.

items.label: list_item
items.text: When the solvent has moved up the paper to about 1 cm from the top, remove the paper from the beaker and draw a pencil line to show where the solvent got to. The highest level of the solvent on the paper at any time is called the solvent front.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Leave the paper to dry so that all the solvent evaporates.

items.label: text
items.text: For the solvent you can use water or a non-aqueous solvent (a solvent other than water). Which solvent you use depends on what substances are present in the mixture. A suitable solvent is usually found by experimenting with different ones.

items.label: text
items.text: The dyes that make up the mixture will be different in two important ways:
